FMA82472.definition: A multicellular structure that is a part of an organ.
FMA82472.description: anatomical structure, each instance of which has as its direct parts some instance of portions of two or more types of tissue and is continuous with some instance of one or more anatomical structures
FMA82472.label: organ part

FMA82485.definition: A part of a wall of an organ that forms a layer.

FMA83115.definition: A structure consisting mainly of cell components, rather than complete cells.

FMA83143.definition: A multi cell part structure that is part of a central nervous system.

FMA83686.definition: A spatially aggregated collection of nerve cell bodies in the CNS, consisting of one or more subpopulations that share cell type, chemical phenotype, and connections, and including nearby cells that share the same cell type, chemical phenotype, and connections. (CUMBO).
isA: central nervous system cell part cluster
FMA83686.description: brain structure consisting of a relatively compact cluster of neurons
FMA83686.label: neural nucleus

FMA83840.definition: A neural nucleus that is part of the brain.

isA: central nervous system cell part cluster

FMA83865.definition: A C-shaped bundle of fibres (axons) in the brain, and carries signals from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies and septal nuclei. It is typically divided into the columns (crus), body, commissure and the pre-commissural and post-commissural fornix (MM).

FMA83874.definition: A ridge on the cerebral cortex. It is generally surrounded by one or more sulci .
FMA83874.description: outward fold on the brain surface
FMA83874.label: gyrus

FMA83906.definition: Axon tract that crosses the midline of the central nervous system[NIF, modified]. In the context of Drosophila refers to a broad band of axons connecting equivalent neuropils each side of the brain.

FMA83929.definition: Neural tissue consisting of myelinated axons connecting grey matter areas of the central nervous system.
isA: central nervous system cell part cluster
FMA83929.label: white matter

FMA83930.definition: A partion of white matter that is part of a telencephalon. This can be further subdivided in some species, for example, into hemisphere white matter and the corpus callosum.
synonyms: predominantly white regional part of telencephalon

FMA83966.definition: The tentorium cerebelli or cerebellar tentorium is an extension of the dura mater that separates the cerebellum from the inferior portion of the occipital lobes.
FMA83966.description: vertebrate brain structure separating the cerebellum from the occipital lobes

FMA84059.definition: Gray matter of the central nervous system which is a collection of clustered nuclei.

FMA84081.definition: Any of any of the secretory or sensory organs located in the brain region around or in relation to the ventricular system that are characterized by extensive vasculature and a lack of a normal blood brain barrier (BBB) and allow for the linkage between the central nervous system and peripheral blood flow.
FMA84081.label: circumventricular organ

synonyms: proximal myotendinous region of muscle organ
FMA85453.label: head of muscle

FMA86140.definition: A part of an organ that constitutes a distinct modular sub-unit. In some cases, the organ may also contain other sub-units of identical or similar types, in other cases this may be a distinct entity.
synonyms: organ region with fixed fiat boundary

FMA86188.definition: A blood vessel that carries blood from the capillaries toward the heart.

FMA86464.definition: White matter structure containing massive numbers of commissural fibers connecting cortical areas in the two cerebral hemispheres. It is subdivided into a genu, a rostrum, a body, and a splenium. (MM).

FMA87217.definition: The part of the aorta that extends from the arch of the aorta to the diaphragm, and from which arises numerous branches that supply oxygenated blood to the chest cage and the organs within the chest.

FMA222905.definition: A section dividing a colon along a proximal-distal axis.

FMA230984.definition: A middle phalanx that is part of a pedal digit 5 [Automatically generated definition].

FMA241998.definition: White matter that is part of a cerebral hemisphere.
synonyms: white matter structure of cerebral hemisphere

FMA242770.definition: A layer in the central nervous system that lines system of communicating cavities in the brain and spinal cord.

FMA256174.definition: White matter that is part of a cerebral hemisphere.
synonyms: white matter structure of cerebral hemisphere

FMA256194.definition: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone. It is divided into four orbital gyri by a well-marked H-shaped orbital sulcus. These are named, from their position, the medial, anterior, lateral, and posterior orbital gyri. The medial orbital gyrus presents a well-marked antero-posterior sulcus, the olfactory sulcus, for the olfactory tract; the portion medial to this is named the straight gyrus, and is continuous with the superior frontal gyrus on the medial surface.

FMA256693.definition: A nucleus of brain that is part of a thalamus.

FMA258714.definition: A dorsal thalamus that is in_the_right_side_of a diencephalon.

FMA258716.definition: A dorsal thalamus that is in_the_left_side_of a diencephalon.

FMA3734.definition: The main trunk of the systemic arterial system that carries blood from the heart to all the organs and other structures of the body, bringing oxygenated blood to all parts of the body in the systemic circulation.

FMA3862.definition: An artery that branches from the left coronary artery and supplies the anterior wall of the left ventricle, the interventricular septum, and the apex of the heart.

FMA7088.definition: A myogenic muscular circulatory organ found in the vertebrate cardiovascular system composed of chambers of cardiac muscle. It is the primary circulatory organ.
isA: structure with developmental contribution from neural crest
FMA7088.label: human heart

FMA7096.definition: A cardiac atrium that is in the right side of the heart. It receives deoxygenated blood. In mammals, this comes from the superior and inferior vena cava and the coronary sinus, and pumps it into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.

FMA7097.definition: A cardiac atrium that is in the left side of the heart. It receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins, In mammals this is pumped into the left ventricle, via the Mitral valve.

FMA7098.definition: A cardiac ventricle that is in the right side of the heart.

FMA7101.definition: A cardiac ventricle that is in the left side of the heart.

FMA7152.definition: Anatomical system that has as its parts the organs devoted to the ingestion, digestion, and assimilation of food and the discharge of residual wastes.
FMA7152.label: human digestive system

FMA7154.definition: The head is the anterior-most division of the body.
isA: subdivision of organism along main body axis
FMA7154.description: anterior anatomical region in many animals, which tends to contain sensory and nervous organs and orifices for ingestion and breathing

FMA7155.definition: An organism subdivision that extends from the head to the pectoral girdle, encompassing the cervical vertebral column.
FMA7155.description: part of the body, on many terrestrial or secondarily aquatic vertebrates, that distinguishes the head from the torso or trunk

FMA7157.definition: The nervous system is an organ system containing predominantly neuron and glial cells. In bilaterally symmetrical organism, it is arranged in a network of tree-like structures connected to a central body. The main functions of the nervous system are to regulate and control body functions, and to receive sensory input, process this information, and generate behavior.
FMA7157.description: part of an animal that coordinates actions and senses

FMA7158.definition: Functional system which consists of structures involved in respiration.
FMA7158.description: system in an organism that exchanges respiratory gases

FMA7159.definition: The renal system in an anatomical system that maintains fluid balance and contributes to electrolyte balance, acid/base balance, and disposal of nitrogenous waste products.

FMA7160.definition: Anatomical system that has as its parts the organs concerned with reproduction.
FMA7160.label: human reproductive system

FMA7161.definition: Anatomical system that has as its parts the heart and blood vessels.
isA: structure with developmental contribution from neural crest
FMA7161.description: three independent systems that work together: cardiovascular, pulmonary and systemic
FMA7161.label: circulatory system

FMA7165.definition: Any chamber of the right side of the heart.
FMA7165.label: right heart

FMA7166.definition: Any chamber of the left side of the heart.
FMA7166.label: left heart

FMA7181.definition: Organism subdivision which is the part of the body posterior to the cervical region (or head, when cervical region not present) and anterior to the caudal region. Includes the sacrum when present.
isA: subdivision of organism along main body axis
FMA7181.description: central part of the living body
FMA7181.label: torso

FMA7184.definition: Appendage girdle complex that when present, encompasses the pelvic appendicular skeleton and the pelvic girdle.
synonyms: pelvic girdle plus pelvic limb or fin
pelvic girdle plus posterior limb or fin
FMA7184.description: region of the lower limb in animals, extending from the gluteal region to the foot, and including the buttocks, hip and leg

FMA7185.definition: A forelimb that is on the right side of a pectoral complex.
FMA7185.description: right arm (hand, forearm, upper arm and shoulder)

FMA7186.definition: A forelimb that is on the left side of a pectoral complex.
FMA7186.description: left arm (hand, forearm, upper arm and shoulder)

FMA7187.definition: A hindlimb that is on the right side of a pelvic complex.

FMA7188.definition: A hindlimb that is on the left side of a pelvic complex.

FMA7197.definition: An exocrine gland which secretes bile and functions in metabolism of protein and carbohydrate and fat, synthesizes substances involved in the clotting of the blood, synthesizes vitamin A, detoxifies poisonous substances, stores glycogen, and breaks down worn-out erythrocytes.

FMA7200.definition: Subdivision of digestive tract that connects the stomach to the large intestine and is where much of the digestion and absorption of food takes place (with the exception of ruminants). The mammalian small intestine is long and coiled and can be differentiated histologically into: duodenum, jejunem, ileum[WP,cjm,Kardong].

FMA7201.definition: A subdivision of the digestive tract that connects the small intestine to the cloaca or anus. Lacks or has few villi.

FMA7208.definition: The portion of the small intestine that extends from the jejunum to the colon.

FMA7235.definition: An atrioventricular valve that is part of the outflow part of the left atrium.

FMA7236.description: valve in the human heart between the left ventricle and the aorta

FMA7246.definition: The semilunar valve of the heart that lies between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery.

FMA7259.definition: A papillary muscle that is part of a right ventricle [Automatically generated definition].

FMA7309.definition: Lung which consists of the right upper lobe, middle lobe and right lower lobe..

FMA7310.definition: Lung which consists of the left upper lobe and left lower lobe..

FMA7333.definition: The lobe of the right lung that is closest to the head.

FMA7337.definition: The lobe of the right lung that is furtherst from the head.

FMA14627.definition: The abdominal wall represents the boundaries of the abdominal cavity. The abdominal wall is split into the posterior (back), lateral (sides) and anterior (front) walls. There is a common set of layers covering and forming all the walls: the deepest being the extraperitoneal fat, the parietal peritoneum, and a layer of fascia which has different names over where it covers (eg transversalis, psoas fascia). Superficial to these, but not present in the posterior wall are the three layers of muscle, the transversus abdominis (transverse abdominal muscle), the internal (obliquus internus) and the external oblique (obliquus externus).

FMA45628.definition: In the circulatory system of animals, a portal venous system occurs when a capillary bed drains into another capillary bed through veins, without first going through the heart. Both capillary beds and the blood vessels that connect them are considered part of the portal venous system. They are relatively uncommon as the majority of capillary beds drain into veins which then drain into the heart, not into another capillary bed. Portal venous systems are considered venous because the blood vessels that join the two capillary beds are either veins or venules. Examples of such systems include the hepatic portal system and the hypophyseal portal system. Unqualified, 'portal venous system' often refers to the hepatic portal system. For this reason, 'portal vein' most commonly refers to the hepatic portal vein.
